name: 3D Bilateral Grid Slicing
definition: A method to approximate color transformations (e.g., ISP) by storing affine transformation matrices in a 3D grid indexed by spatial coordinates (x, y) and color guidance (grayscale intensity). It solves the problem of view-dependent color correction by learning a continuous function mapping pixel coordinates and colors to affine matrices.
summary: 3D Bilateral Grid Slicing approximates view-dependent color corrections in neural radiance fields by storing affine matrices in a 3D grid indexed by spatial and color coordinates.
